senses.definition: a car

examples.x: the auto industry

senses.definition: a narrow road in the country

examples.x: winding country lanes
We drove along a muddy lane to reach the farmhouse.

senses.definition: a city street

examples.x: Park Lane
The quickest way is through the back lanes behind the bus station.

senses.definition: a section of a wide road, that is marked by painted white lines, to keep lines of traffic separate

examples.x: the inside/middle lane
the northbound/southbound lane
to change lanes
a four-lane highway

senses.definition: a narrow marked section of a track or a swimming pool that is used by one person, for example when taking part in a race

examples.x: The Australian in lane four is coming up fast from behind.
Obi, the record holder, is in lane 3.

senses.definition: a route used by ships or aircraft on regular journeys

examples.x: one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes

senses.definition: (in tenpin bowling) a narrow section of floor along which the ball is bowled

examples.x: a 20-lane bowling alley

senses.definition: where things are most exciting and where a lot is happening

examples.x: He had a good job, plenty of money and he was enjoying life in the fast lane.

senses.definition: something that is being carried (usually in large amounts) by a person, vehicle, etc.

examples.x: The trucks waited at the warehouse to pick up their loads.
The women came down the hill with their loads of firewood.
These backpacks are designed to carry a heavy load.
A lorry shed its load (= accidentally dropped its load) on the motorway.
The company's debt load could drag it into bankruptcy.

senses.definition: the total amount of something that something can carry or contain

examples.x: a busload of tourists
They ordered three truckloads of sand.
He put half a load of washing in the machine.
The plane took off with a full load.
Maximum load, including passengers, is 800 pounds.

senses.definition: the amount of weight that is pressing down on something

examples.x: a load-bearing wall
Modern backpacks spread the load over a wider area.
The table creaked under its heavy load.

senses.definition: a large number or amount of people or things; plenty

examples.x: She's got loads of friends.
He wrote loads and loads of letters to people.
Uncle Jim brought a whole load of presents for the kids.
We saw a load of houses before we bought this one.
They all had loads of fun at the park.
In my job I get the chance to meet loads of different people.
There's loads to do today.

senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is wrong, stupid, bad, etc.

examples.x: You're talking a load of rubbish.

senses.definition: an amount of work that a person or machine has to do

examples.x: Teaching loads have increased in all types of school.
Extra warmth from sunlight can put an additional load on the air-conditioning system.
We're trying to spread the load by employing more staff.

senses.definition: a feeling of responsibility or worry that is difficult to deal with

examples.x: She thought she would not be able to bear the load of bringing up her family alone.
Knowing that they had arrived safely took a load off my mind.

senses.definition: the amount of electrical power that is being supplied at a particular time
used to tell somebody to look at or listen to somebody/something

examples.x: Get a load of that dress!

senses.definition: a large vehicle for carrying heavy loads by road

examples.x: a lorry driver
a lorry load of frozen fish
Emergency food supplies were brought in by lorry.

senses.definition: goods that fell off the back of a lorry were probably stolen. People say or accept that they came ‘off the back of a lorry’ to avoid saying or asking where they really came from.
the ability to move easily from one place, social class or job to another

examples.x: social/geographical/career mobility
The high cost of living acts as an obstacle to mobility of labour.

senses.definition: the ability to move or travel around easily

examples.x: An electric wheelchair has given her greater mobility.
mobility training for blind people

senses.definition: having an engine; using the power of an engine

examples.x: The street is closed to motor vehicles.

senses.definition: connected with vehicles that have engines

examples.x: Europe's motor industry faces international competition.
I like all forms of motor sports.
a motor accident
motor insurance
motor fuel

senses.definition: connected with movement of the body that is produced by muscles; connected with the nerves that control movement

examples.x: uncoordinated motor activity
Both motor and sensory functions are affected.

senses.definition: a road vehicle with two wheels, driven by an engine, with one seat for the driver and often a seat for a passenger behind the driver

examples.x: He never learned to ride a motorcycle or to drive a car.
She rode round Italy on a motorcycle.
motorcycle racing
a motorcycle accident
The car was accompanied by a police motorcycle escort.

senses.definition: a person driving a car

examples.x: The accident was reported by a passing motorist.
Motorists who fail to stop risk an even higher penalty.

senses.definition: the skill or the process of planning a route for a ship or other vehicle and taking it there

examples.x: an expert in navigation
a GPS navigation device
The stars were used for navigation in the desert.

senses.definition: the movement of ships or aircraft

examples.x: the right of navigation through international waters

senses.definition: the way that you move around a website or the internet when you are looking for information

examples.x: The site was redesigned to improve navigation.

senses.definition: the act of stopping a vehicle at a place and leaving it there for a period of time

examples.x: There is no parking here between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m.
I managed to find a parking space.
I got there early to grab a parking spot.
I pulled the car over into a parking bay.
a parking fine (= for parking illegally)

senses.definition: a space or an area for leaving vehicles

examples.x: The hotel is centrally situated with ample free parking.
parking for 300 cars
There is off-street parking at the front of the house.
The town has free on-street parking.
The public did not vote for increased car parking charges.
The hotel has six levels of underground parking.

senses.definition: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train, plane or ship and who is not driving it or working on it

examples.x: airline/cruise/rail/bus passengers
I soon got talking to a fellow passenger on the flight.
The boat was carrying more than 100 passengers.
a passenger train (= carrying passengers, not goods)

senses.definition: a member of a group or team who does not do as much work as the others

examples.x: The firm cannot afford to carry passengers.

senses.definition: a liquid obtained from petroleum, used as fuel in car engines, etc.

examples.x: to fill a car up with petrol
to run out of petrol
The car has a 2-litre petrol engine.
the petrol tank of a car
An increase in petrol prices will lead to severe difficulties for the company.
leaded/unleaded petrol

senses.definition: a flying vehicle with wings and one or more engines

examples.x: a passenger/fighter/military/private plane
They boarded the plane and flew to Chicago.
I caught the next plane to Dublin.
The plane took off an hour late.
The plane landed in Geneva.
to fly a plane
She left by plane for Berlin.
a plane ticket
a plane crash
a plane ride/flight/journey

senses.definition: any flat or level surface, or an imaginary flat surface through or joining material objects

examples.x: the horizontal/vertical plane
We may describe uniquely any point in a plane by an ordered pair of numbers, called coordinates.

senses.definition: a level of thought, existence or development

examples.x: With practice, an athlete can reach a higher plane of achievement.
They seem to exist on a different spiritual plane.
Like all talented musicians, he operates on a different plane from most people.

senses.definition: a tool with a blade (= sharp metal part) set in a flat surface, used for making the surface of wood smooth by cutting very thin layers off it
a town or city with a harbour, especially one where ships load and unload goods

examples.x: a container/fishing port
Rotterdam is a major port.
the port city of Gdansk
the Black Sea ports

senses.definition: a place where ships load and unload goods or shelter from storms

examples.x: a naval port
a container/ferry port
The ship spent four days in port.
They reached port at last.
port of entry (= a place where people or goods can enter a country)
the port authorities

senses.definition: a strong sweet wine, usually dark red, that is made in Portugal. It is usually drunk at the end of a meal.
a glass of port
the side of a ship or aircraft that is on the left when you are facing forward

examples.x: the port side

senses.definition: a place on a computer where you can attach another piece of equipment, often using a cable

examples.x: the modem port

senses.definition: if you are in great trouble, you take any help that is offered
